If the figure above shows the graph of $g(x),$ then

${lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{g(x)}{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-7}=$

 {{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
From the diagram, ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }g(x)=-2.$

Now, rewrite the target limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{g(x)}{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-7} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }g(x)\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-7}\end{aligned}
$$

For any non-constant polynomial $P(x),$ we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \pm \infty }(\frac{1}{P(x)})=0.
$$

Therefore, since ${x}^{3}$ is a non-constant polynomial, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-7}=0.
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the original limit as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }g(x)\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-7}=-2\cdot 0=0\end{aligned}
$$
